t: The next to the last sentence of subsection (c) of section 8 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act is amended by striking out the period at the end thereof and inserting in lieu thereof a comma and the following: “except that in the case of any project on which construction was initiated in such State after June 30, 1966, which was approved by the appropriate State water pollution control agency and which the Secretary finds meets the requirements of this section but was constructed without such assistance, such allotments for any fiscal year ending prior to July 1, 1971, shall also be available for payments in reimbursement of State or local funds used for such project prior to July 1, 1971, to the extent that assistance could have been provided under this section if such project had been approved pursuant to this section and adequate funds had been available. In the case of any project on which construction was initiated in such State after June 30, 1966, and which was constructed with assistance pursuant to this section but the amount of such assistance was a lesser per centum of the cost of construction than was allowable pursuant to this section, such allotments shall also be available for payments in reimbursement of State or local funds used for such project prior to July 1, 1971, to the extent that assistance could have been provided under this section if adequate funds had been available. Neither a finding by the Secretary that a project meets the requirements of this subsection, nor any other provision of this subsection, shall be con-strued to constitute a commitment or obligation of the United States to provide funds to make or pay any grant for such project.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that approval by the State water pollution control agency amounts to federal-state coordination. That approval is only an eligibility condition for reimbursing State or local funds spent on projects built without federal assistance; it is a grant-funding rule, not a process for consulting outsiders before a federal decision. The section creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: which was approved by the appropriate State water pollution control agency and which the Secretary finds meets the requirements of this section

qwen_block.w: This section describes the eligibility criteria for state and local governments to receive reimbursement for water pollution control projects. It details the conditions under which the Secretary of the Interior may approve projects for funding, but it does not require the federal government to consult with outside parties before making that decision. The text explicitly states that the Secretary's finding does not constitute a commitment to provide funds, reinforcing that this is a grant application/reimbursement process rather than a participatory decision-making process involving public input or advisory bodies.
qwen_block.s: Neither a finding by the Secretary that a project meets the requirements of this subsection, nor any other provision of this subsection, shall be con-strued to constitute a commitment or obligation of the United States to provide funds to make or pay any grant for such project.

opus.w: This amendment sets when federal water-pollution grant allotments can reimburse state or local funds already spent on construction projects. That is a grant and funding eligibility rule, which the definition excludes. The tempting reading treats the state water pollution control agency's approval as participation. But that approval concerns the state's own project, and nothing in the section requires the Secretary to consult outside parties before making a federal decision.
opus.s: such allotments for any fiscal year ending prior to July 1, 1971, shall also be available for payments in reimbursement of State or local funds used for such project prior to July 1, 1971
opus.b:
**Step 1: The tempting reading.** The provision refers to a project "approved by the appropriate State water pollution control agency," so a non-federal body plays a role before federal money is paid out. That could look like a state taking part in a federal decision.

**Why it fails:** The state agency is approving its own state or local construction project. It is not being consulted on a federal policy. The section only decides whether federal grant allotments can reimburse state or local funds already spent. Grant and benefit eligibility is expressly excluded from the definition of participation. The section also has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes conditions under which state or local funds can be reimbursed by the federal government. The requirement for state agency approval is part of the eligibility criteria for receiving these funds (a grant/reimbursement mechanism). The definition explicitly states that participation 'does not include applications for benefits or grants.' Therefore, this is not participation.
qwen_chat.s: which was approved by the appropriate State water pollution control agency and which the Secretary finds meets the requirements of this section but was constructed without such assistance, such allotments for any fiscal year ending prior to July 1, 1971, shall also be available for payments in reimbursement of State or local funds used for such project
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions that projects must be "approved by the appropriate State water pollution control agency."
Resolution: This approval is a condition for the state/local entity to receive federal reimbursement funds. It is part of the application/grant process, not a requirement for the federal government to consult with outsiders before making a policy decision. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants.
